source_text: non pro causis esse mutandam, quod ipsa dona sua pro accidentium capacitate dispensat. Ideoque Christus qui est sui operis redemptor, auget circa imaginem suam continua largitate beneficia; et quos fecerat condendo bonos, facit innovando adoptandoque meliores gratiam Baptismatis
pass_a_gloss: Not for causis to-be mutandam, that/which herself gifts his-own for accidentium capacitate dispensat. for-that-reason-and Christ who is of-himself of-the-work redeemer, auget around image his-own continua by-bounty benefits; and whom fecerat by-creating good, makes by-renewing by-adopting-and better grace of-baptism.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: The grace of baptism need not be changed according to the circumstances, since it distributes its own gifts according to the capacity of those who come to it. So Christ, who is the redeemer of his own work, continually increases his gifts to his image with generous kindness. Those whom he made good by creating them, he makes better by renewing and adopting them.

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
